quote: 1. The best stock to buy may be the one you already own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 2. Just because you buy a stock and it goes up does not mean you are right. Just because you buy a stock and it goes down does not mean you are wrong.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 3. If you don't study any companies you have the same chance of success buying stocks as you do in a poker game if you bet without looking at your cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 4. Know what you own, and know why you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 5. You should not buy a stock because it's cheap but because you know a lot about it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 6. Avoid long shots. I've bought about 30 long shots in my life. I've never broken even on one.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 7. In this business if you're good, you're right six times out of ten. You're never going to be right nine times out of ten.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 8. Everyone has the brainpower to make money in stocks. Not everyone has the stomach. If you are susceptible to selling everything in a panic, you ought to avoid stocks and mutual funds altogether.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 9. The worst thing you can do is invest in companies you know nothing about. Unfortunately, buying stocks on ignorance is still a popular American pastime.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 10. I deal in facts, not forecasting the future. That's crystal ball stuff.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 11. The stock market demands conviction as surely as it victimizes the unconvinced.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 12. Owning stocks is like having children — don't get involved with more than you can handle.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 13. Absent a lot of surprises, stocks are relatively predictable over 10 to 20 years. As to whether they're going to be higher or lower in 2 or 3 years, you might as well flip a coin to decide.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 14. The person that turns over the most rocks wins the game. And that's always been my philosophy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 15. When even the analysts at the brokerage houses ignore a stock, the astute investor gets an opportunity to buy a bargain.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 16. All you need for a lifetime of successful investing is a few big winners, and the willingness not to interfere with them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 17. Every once in a while, the market does something so stupid it takes your breath away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 18. A cocktail party can be a useful stock market indicator.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 19. The p/e ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 20. Buy what you know.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 21. Gentlemen who prefer bonds don't know what they're missing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 22. You can't see the future through a rearview mirror.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 23. When you sell in desperation, you always sell cheap.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 24. There is always something to worry about. Avoid weekend thinking and ignoring the latest dire predictions of the newscasters. Sell a stock because the company's fundamentals deteriorate, not because the sky is falling.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 25. Never invest in any idea you can't illustrate with a crayon.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 26. You don't have to be a rocket scientist. Investing is not a game where the guy with the 160 IQ beats the guy with the 130 IQ.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 27. The stock market isn't a casino, but you can turn it into one if you play switch the pig.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 28. If you stay half-alert, you can pick the spectacular performers right from your place of business or out of the neighborhood shopping mall, and long before Wall Street discovers them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 29. Behind every stock is a company. Find out what it's doing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 30. Debt is saving in reverse. The more it builds up, the worse off you are.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 31. Nobody can predict interest rates, the future direction of the economy or the stock market. Dismiss all such forecasts and concentrate on what's actually happening to the companies in which you've invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 32. Average investors can become experts in their own field and can pick winning stocks as effectively as Wall Street professionals by doing just a little research.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 33. If you can't convince yourself "When I'm down 25 percent, I'm a buyer" and banish forever the fatal thought "When I'm down 25 percent, I'm a seller," then you'll never make a decent profit in stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 34. If you like the store, chances are you'll love the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 35. Corporations, like people, change their names for one of two reasons: either they've gotten married, or they've been involved in some fiasco that they hope the public will forget.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 36. You can beat the market by ignoring the herd.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 37. If you can't explain to an 11-year-old in two minutes or less why you own the stock, you shouldn't own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 38. In dieting and in stocks, it is the gut and not the head that determines the results.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 39. Insiders might sell their shares for any number of reasons, but they buy them for only one: they think the price will rise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 40. There's no shame in losing money on a stock. Everybody does it. What is shameful is to hold onto a stock, or worse, to buy more of it, when the fundamentals are deteriorating.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 41. The best time to invest is when you have money. This is because history suggests it is not timing which matters, it is time.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 42. In stocks, as in romance, ease of divorce is not grounds for getting married.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 43. Time is on your side when you own shares of superior companies.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 44. Selling your winners and holding your losers is like cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 45. If you spend more than 13 minutes analyzing economic and market forecasts, you've wasted 10 minutes.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 46. Big companies have small moves, small companies have big moves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 47. In the stock market, time is your friend, and impulse is your enemy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 48. Never bet on a comeback while they're playing "Taps."
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 49. The real key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 50. If you can't understand the balance sheet, you probably shouldn't own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 51. Never invest in any company before you've done the homework on the company's earnings prospects, financial condition, competitive position, plans for expansion, and so forth.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 52. There's no point paying Yo-Yo Ma to play a radio.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 53. If you are thinking of investing in a troubled industry, buy the companies with staying power. Also, wait for the industry to show signs of revival. Buggy whips and radio tubes were troubled industries that never came back.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 54. Never invest in a company without understanding its finances. The biggest losses in stocks come from companies with poor balance sheets. Always look at the balance sheet to see if a company is solvent before you risk your money on it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 55. In Wall Street parlance, a 'tenbagger' is a stock in which you've made ten times your money.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 56. The public's careful when they buy a house, when they buy a refrigerator, when they buy a car. They'll work hours to save a hundred dollars on a roundtrip air ticket. Yet they'll put $5,000 or $10,000 on some zany idea they heard on the bus. That's gambling. That's not investing. That's not research. That's just total speculation.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 57. The best place to begin looking for the tenbagger is close to home—if not in the backyard then down at the shopping mall, and especially wherever you happen to work.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 58. The extra 5 minutes you spend deciding whether to buy a hot stock will save you the 10 years it takes recouping your losses.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 59. A stock-market decline is as routine as a January blizzard in Colorado. If you're prepared for it, the storm won't hurt you.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 60. Gambling successfully on economic trends is one of the most difficult things to do consistently, and I don't know anyone who has done it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 61. Charts are great for predicting the past.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 62. The stocks that have been most rewarding to me have made their greatest gains in the third or fourth year I owned them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 63. Although it's easy to forget sometimes, a share of stock is not a lottery ticket. It's part ownership of a business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 64. You need an edge to make money, too. People have incredible edges and they throw them away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 65. The secret is if you have a lot of stocks, some will do mediocre, some will do okay, and if one or two of them go up big time, you produce a fabulous result.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 66. The stock market's been the best place to be over the last 10 years, 30 years, 100 years. But if you need money in 1 or 2 years, you shouldn't be buying stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 67. In the long run, a portfolio of well-chosen stocks and/or equity mutual funds will always outperform a portfolio of bonds or a money-market account.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 68. If a fund manager is right six times out of ten, he or she is having a very good year.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 69. Among the qualities you need are: patience, self-reliance, common sense, a tolerance for pain, open-mindedness, detachment, persistence, humility, flexibility, a willingness to do independent research, an equal willingness to admit to mistakes, and the ability to ignore general panic.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 70. Any normal person using the customary three percent of the brain can pick stocks just as well, if not better, than the average Wall Street expert.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 71. Everyone has the brainpower to follow the stock market. If you made it through fifth-grade math, you can do it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 72. A price drop in a good stock is only a tragedy if you sell at that price and never buy more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 73. Often, there is no correlation between the success of a company's operations and the success of its stock over a few months or even a few years. In the long term, there is a 100 percent correlation between the success of the company and the success of its stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 74. You have to know what you own, and why you own it. "This baby is a cinch to go up" doesn't count.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 75. This is where it helps to have identified your personal investor's edge. What is it that you know a lot about? Maybe your edge comes from your profession or a hobby. Maybe it comes just from being a parent.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 76. I'm always on the lookout for great companies in lousy industries.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 77. It's impossible to time the market, let alone individual stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 78. In every industry and every region of the country, the observant amateur can find great growth companies long before the professionals have discovered them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 79. An important key to investing is to remember that stocks are not lottery tickets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 80. I can't imagine anything that's useful to know that the amateur investor can't find out.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 81. Stand by your stocks as long as the fundamental story of the company hasn't changed.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 82. You have to say to yourself, "If I'm right, how much am I going to make? If I'm wrong, how much am I going to lose?" That's the risk/reward ratio.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 83. If you don't believe corporate profits will continue to rise, and you can't stomach a decline in the market, don't buy stocks or equity mutual funds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 84. During a lifetime of eating donuts or buying tires, I've developed a feel for the product line that I'll never have with laser beams or microprocessors.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 85. If you can't find any companies that you think are attractive, put your money in the bank until you discover some.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 86. Searching for companies is like looking for grubs under rocks: if you turn over 10 rocks you'll likely find one grub; if you turn over 20 rocks you'll find two.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 87. If you invest $1,000 in a stock, all you can lose is $1,000, but you stand to gain $10,000 or even $50,000 over time if you're patient.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 88. People who succeed in the stock market also accept periodic losses, setbacks, and unexpected occurrences. Calamitous drops do not scare them out of the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 89. Go for a business that any idiot can run - because sooner or later, any idiot probably is going to run it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 90. Companies that have no debt can't go bankrupt.
speaker: Peter Lynch
